etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Ancient Greek γιγαντικός (gigantikós), ultimately from γίγας (gígas, “giant”). According to the Poly-Olbion project coined by Michael Drayton in 1612.

quote.text: Thou Genius of the place (this most renowned Ile)Which livedst long before the All-earth-drowning Flood,Whilst yet the world did swarme with her Gigantick brood;

quote.citation: 1834, L[etitia] E[lizabeth] L[andon], chapter XXXII, in Francesca Carrara. […], volume III, London: Richard Bentley, […], (successor to Henry Colburn), →OCLC, page 259:
quote.text: It is in solitude that the imagination exercises its gigantic power; and where are a woman's feelings nurtured but in solitude?

definitions.definition: In the manner of a giant. (Can we add an example for this sense?)
